- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and forecast remains high, apply downward bias of 3–5% to reflect market cooling.  
- Forecasting 30-day ahead: if recent 5-day average is falling, model should not overshoot below 10% of the 5-day low.  
- If forecast shows a sharp upward move after a recent dip, check for mean reversion — cap the rise at 1.5x recent high if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3–0.7), avoid extrapolating trends — use 3–5 day smoothing to reduce noise-driven overcorrection.  
- If forecast is consistently 5–8% above true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, apply a 2–3% downward correction to prevent overconfidence bias.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down, assume mean reversion and adjust forecast to align with 10–15% below recent peak.
